mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the trigger period, or the 5.25% threshold is not clearly crossed (e.g., 5.24%).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% in a month coincides with easing labor market pressures, prompting market expectations of corporate cost-cutting and thus a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or UNRATE remains above 4% for at least 3 consecutive months post-trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) above 1,300 leads to anticipatory equity price appreciation, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (p > 0.05) in the 20-day window following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108 signals supply-side weakness, reducing investor confidence and producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-negative during the contraction period, or INDPRO recovers to 108 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months indicate deflationary expectations, which compress real discount rates and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return advantage (p > 0.10) during the 3-month deflation window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (PAYEMS) above 150,000 coincides with labor market loosening, prompting expectations of wage growth and a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative or job openings remain below 150,000 for the next 3 days.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) signal dual weakening in labor and supply, amplifying market uncertainty and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or either proxy recovers to neutral/strong levels within the window.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged expansionary monetary policy regime (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), S&P 500 60-day forward returns tend to be positive due to higher investor risk appetite, regardless of other macro variables.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in > 40% of months with FEDFUNDS < 1.5% over a 3-year window.
